anti_requirements: No independent claim audit, proof requirement, research assignment, claim-risk report, or claim-approval gate may be added. Claim verification, substantiation, and approval belong to the human reviewer.
Self-ratings must not be printed in the client handoff.

qualitative_rules.rule: Pain sections are second-person statements; no question-led pain framing. HARD in the guide, but question classification is heuristic: the validator flags candidate question sentences and the reviewer confirms.
qualitative_rules.source: Section 2-4 lessons; 'Source tensions' (sample deviations and the historical screenshots' questions do not override the written rule)

qualitative_rules.rule: The Section 5 body opens with 'That is the reason why', 'That is why', or a natural equivalent. The two named forms are mechanically checkable; a natural equivalent is an either/or judgment the reviewer confirms.
Each pain is a distinct pressure point; a synonym of an earlier pain fails. The matched solution is not merged into a standard pain (solutions are long-form 2A/3A/4A).
Each persona entry pairs a relevant person or situation with a recognized pain OR a desired outcome (either/or). Job titles or profession lists alone fail.
Inclusions are named, concrete items (session, exercise, tool, experience, access, deliverable), each with an immediate use, and only inclusions from the client brief.
Three distinct payoffs; a benefit that repeats an inclusion, a pain, or another benefit fails.

Part 5 (The Big Invite) names the same offer and participation action as Section 1. Mechanical prefilter: when the copy manifest declares offer_name, the validator checks its presence in Section 1 and in Part 5 and flags its absence; action equivalence remains reviewer judgment.
The assembled page contains no invented bonus, video button, guarantee, timer, audience-exclusion section, or testimonial block.
